clue.text: A truly heavenly picture

parts.note: a 'heavenly' picture is read literally: not a divine painting but a view of the heavens themselves, a painting of clouds and sky

explanation.definitionFit: A painting or view whose subject is the sky is a picture of the heavens in the most literal sense.

clue.text: An engineer getting papers mixed up

indicators.note: mixed up says the letters of the word papers are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An engineer has got documents muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed up' rearranges PAPERS. A sapper is a soldier in the Royal Engineers, the British Army's combat engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A military field engineer who digs trenches and lays or clears mines is called by this name.

clue.text: The archaic warning given by royal bodyguard

definitions.note: the definition is a collective noun for a body of guards, matching the plural answer

parts.note: ye is the old-fashioned spelling of the word 'the'
an omen is a portent or warning sign

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned caution is issued by the monarch's protectors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yeomen of the Guard are the British sovereign's ceremonial bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yeomen of the Guard form the British monarch's ceremonial guard, so the members collectively are that guard.

clue.text: Figures in French church to lay hands on

parts.note: C and L are Roman numerals, 100 and 50
en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: Numbers inside a French church are there to be touched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' looks like statues in the church, but it gives the Roman numerals CL.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip something tightly is to take firm hold of it with the hands.

clue.text: The building is, repeat is, a cake-shop

indicators.note: building, in the sense of constructing, says the words that follow are assembled into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stammers that a certain building is a bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The building' seems to be the subject, but 'building' is the anagram signal: rearrange the ten letters of IS, REPEAT and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-style shop selling pastries and gateaux is the sort of place meant by a cake-shop.

clue.text: Having a cereal in addition costs!

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: PS (postscript) is an addition to a letter
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: An exclamation that adding grain makes things expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'addition' is PS, the postscript added to a letter, with RICE placed in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices are what goods cost, so the plural noun stands for the charges asked.

clue.text: Reasonable 20-a pound!

parts.note: refers to the answer at 20 down, an allowance
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A cross-reference claims a portion is worth a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 refers to the answer of clue 20, which is followed by A and L for pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sensible and in line with logic is reasonable.

clue.text: The firm can't hold onto a good man

indicators.note: hold says the word can't wraps around the pieces that follow

parts.note: the clue word written without its apostrophe
onto is taken as on, with a link to
ST, saint, is a crossword convention for a good man

explanation.surface: A company cannot retain a decent employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The firm' looks like a business, but it is the adjective meaning steady. 'hold' puts ON and ST inside CANT after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast and unwavering: something firm stays fixed and does not change.

clue.text: Play for a number in tranquil fashion

definitions.text: Play for a number in tranquil fashion

parts.words: Play for a number in tranquil fashion
parts.note: describes a gentle piece of music played, often at night beneath a window, for a loved one

explanation.definitionFit: This kind of song is a calm piece performed in tribute, as a lover sings beneath a window at evening.

clue.text: Real estate of quality

definitions.meaning: land and buildings owned by someone
a characteristic attribute, as in the properties of a metal

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both owned land and buildings and an attribute or characteristic of a thing.

clue.text: He's giving satisfaction -models are not

indicators.note: models, used as a verb meaning shapes or fashions, says the words are refashioned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is pleasing others, unlike fashion models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' looks like a noun for fashion figures, but it is a verb, reshaping ARE NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends is to give satisfaction for a wrong, so one who makes amends is giving satisfaction.

clue.text: Practice drill

definitions.meaning: a task done to train or develop skill
a routine of repeated training, as soldiers do

explanation.definitionFit: Both words name repeated training activity, such as a workout or a military routine.

clue.text: Continue to run a place in Lancashire

parts.note: to bolt is to run away suddenly
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: Carrying on running towards a town in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolton is a town near Manchester, historically in the county of Lancashire in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolton is a large town historically in Lancashire, now in Greater Manchester.

clue.text: Set right way — with the grain in line

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

indicators.note: in line says the words are rearranged, lined up afresh in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A carpenter sets wood the correct way, following the grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in line' rearranges THE GRAIN to RAIGHTEN, placed after ST for street.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct something or put it in order is to set it right.

clue.text: About a quarter took a course-so prudent

parts.note: re means about or concerning
S, south, is one quarter of the compass
trained means studied or took a course of instruction

explanation.surface: Someone sensibly went on a training course nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' is a compass point, here S for south.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing moderation and self-control is a sign of a cautious, sensible nature.

clue.text: A person of some conviction

parts.note: conviction reads as firm belief, but here means a guilty verdict in court, leading to a cell

explanation.definitionFit: Someone convicted of a crime and held in jail has a conviction in the legal sense.

clue.text: 4's customers may well call for good order

definitions.text: 4's customers may well call for good order

parts.words: 4's customers may well call for good order
parts.note: 4 is the answer at 4 down, a cake-shop; its customers ask for a pastry dessert, whose name also forms a phrase for neatness

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'in apple-pie order' means perfectly neat and tidy; customers in a cake-shop might order that dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: The dessert's name is also used in a set phrase meaning perfectly neat, so it fits both an order at a bakery and tidiness.

clue.text: A gallant holding back is so wearing!

indicators.note: holding says the word for gallant contains the next piece

parts.note: brave means gallant

indicators.note: back says the word is is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A courageous person's reticence is exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IS into SI, which 'holding' puts inside BRAVE, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrasive grinds and wears away surfaces, or wears on a person's patience.

clue.text: Anti-monarchist bar-keeper after serving men

indicators.note: after says the publican piece comes after the soldiers' abbreviation

parts.note: RE, Royal Engineers, are serving soldiers
a publican keeps a bar in a pub

explanation.surface: A pub landlord with anti-royal views follows soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who favours a state without a king or queen opposes monarchy.

clue.text: The man's into fibre-he'll share whatever's left

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the fibre word

parts.note: coir is coconut fibre
he, with the apostrophe s read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A man goes into the rope trade, sharing an inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: COIR is the fibre from coconut husks used for matting.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint inheritor divides an estate with others, sharing what a dead person bequeaths.

clue.text: Allowance for a rascal inside admitting nothing

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel or rascal

indicators.note: admitting says the word for inside lets the next letter in

parts.note: in means inside
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A scoundrel in prison gets a ration without admitting anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like slang for in prison, but it simply gives IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed portion or share issued to each person is an allowance.

clue.text: Write-up not taken in by one immediately

indicators.note: taken in by says the reversed word sits inside the word for one

parts.note: an ace is one, in cards or dice

indicators.note: in a down clue write-up says the word not is written upwards, in reverse

explanation.surface: A review was not believed by someone straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Write-up' looks like a review, but tells you to write NOT upwards (reversed) as TON, which goes inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without delay is doing it right now, straight away.

clue.text: The potentate's aunt's possibly about fifty

definitions.note: the apostrophe s is read as 'is', linking the definition

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go around the next piece
possibly says the letters of aunt's could be arranged differently

parts.note: the letters of the word, with its s
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A ruler's aunt is perhaps around fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AUNTS to SUTAN, and 'about' puts it around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim sovereign ruler holds absolute power, which makes him a potentate.

clue.text: Rating on in a frenzy, knowing no better

indicators.note: in a frenzy says the letters of rating on are thrown into wild disorder

explanation.surface: A sailor carrying on wildly, unaware of how to behave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rating' looks like a sailor, but its letters with ON are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking knowledge or education knows no better.

clue.text: Sleep the family on the dining-table!

definitions.note: the definition is an item found on the table rather than a noun synonym

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
kin means relatives or family

explanation.surface: The relatives dozing at the dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth square for wiping the mouth is laid at each place on the table.

clue.text: Articles turned in by an urban Greek

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: turned says the word in is turned around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Grammatical articles handed in by a city-dwelling Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' gives two pieces, A and THE; 'turned' makes NI from IN, then AN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Athens, Greece's capital city, is a Greek who lives in a city.

clue.text: Exceptionally severe old magistrates

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests the letters of severe are set out in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Stern judges of a bygone age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptionally' rearranges SEVERE. A reeve was a local official or magistrate in medieval England.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval England these officials administered a district or manor and acted as local magistrates.

clue.text: Send for a gate

definitions.meaning: to send someone is to thrill or enchant them, as in 'that music sends me'

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to delight or captivate; as a noun, a gate or door through which one passes.
